newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Monday due to a strong performance by domestic A shares, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rocketed to 15.45 percent from 3.6 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose sharply to 11.48 million lots from 6.32 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said a continued bull run on the A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen boosted fund demand on the repo market.

The issue of Qianjiang Shenghua Co, an A share company which produces pharmaceuticals, on the Shanghai stock exchange on Monday also pushed institutions to borrow more money, pushing up the repo rates, especially the three-day contract, they said.

"The repo rates will continue to rise in the next few days because of a large number of new A share issues on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses this week," said one trader. "Early-maturing contracts will be more active."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Monday with rising A share markets sucking funds out of the spot market, traders said.
The most active three-year bond that matured in August 1999 fell slightly to 104.88 yuan from 105.17 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.08 million lots from 1.22 million lots.
Traders said the bull run on the A share markets in the past few weeks had hit the spot market with liquidity flowing out.
A large number of new A share issues will further dampen sentiment on the spot market, they said.
"The spot contracts are likely to continue to fall in the short term," one trader said.
